trigger: the deviation-channel machine check says a straight/local-offset deviation is INFEASIBLE for all five residuals => a bent re-route (a router step) is required.

proposed_new_means.name: TARGETED SINGLE-NET RIP-UP + RE-ROUTE (bounded)
proposed_new_means.what: for each residual: freeze the rest of the board, RIP the named blocking segment(s) inside the residual's corridor, route the residual with the in-register maze (bounded to the corridor, FINE_STEP), then RE-ROUTE the ripped net(s) around it; the final DRC + the landing no-isolated-copper gate still adjudicate.
proposed_new_means.why_principled: the residual wall is a routing-COMPETITION/order artefact (the blockers are copper the maze itself laid), so NEGOTIATED rip-up - not more space - is the matching remedy; the supervisor's own #K2-416 note pinned the cause as 'order and yielding'.
proposed_new_means.determinism: bounded to the named blocker(s) and the corridor; one rip/re-route pass per residual (no parameter search, no iteration).

sec20_three_questions.Q1_same_kind_product: YES - 'rip-up and reroute' (R&R) is the standard negotiated-congestion method in every commercial router; the same-chip TI DS320PR1601 EVM drawings (registered, read-only) remain the board-level reference.
sec20_three_questions.Q2_copyable_artifact: YES, IN-REPO - tools/k2_reroute_affected_v2.py (C17 v1: rip -> islands -> stitch -> snap -> repair -> normalise) is the registered rip-up pipeline; eda_eng/ripup.py carries the engine-side rip; the maze (k2_p4_mroute_v1.py) is the router.
sec20_three_questions.Q3_difference_list: our pass must be BOUNDED (one net + its corridor), SINGLE-PASS (no global reshuffle / no iteration), and must keep C2 clean (no new classes) with the landing gate intact; the vendor/C17 pipelines reshuffle globally.
